A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CB-KNN SLAM work. All nine pages of v1 and seventeen pages of v2 are readable, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracking, rendering, relative-pose-error and runtime results on Replica, TUM-RGBD and ScanNet.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, MonoGS integration results and convergence measurements.

M1.justification: The core temporary position/color smoothing, adaptive K and keyframe application remain. The stated densification rule changes from an additive mask using L1(D(p)) in v1 Eq. (9) to a binary indicator maximum using the explicit depth residual in v2 Eq. (11). This is a limited correction to the specified computation; broader implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: The same three indoor RGB-D datasets remain. New evaluated environments include TUM fr1/desk2 and fr1/room and ScanNet 0059. ScanNet 0207 already appeared in v1's trajectory analysis. The explicit novel-view evaluation disappears, and real-data rendering coverage contracts from broad scene comparisons to two ablation sequences.

E2.justification: Tracking comparisons add iMAP, GS-SLAM and Hier-SLAM in the applicable datasets and remove ESLAM. MonoGS and Co-SLAM acquire ScanNet comparison results where v1 had none. Replica rendering adds Co-SLAM and GS-SLAM, substantially changing comparator membership beyond merely extending existing comparisons to additional scenes.

E3.justification: The supplementary evaluation design changes substantially: v2 introduces MonoGS integration on four Replica and three TUM sequences, four position/color configurations on two sequences, and tracking loss versus iteration. It removes v1's selected-frame RPE protocol, using 50 or 100 frames, and separate novel/training-view evaluation. The principal tracking and rendering metrics remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds component isolation testing position versus color smoothing, transfer to MonoGS, convergence analysis and artifact-focused rendering closeups (Tables 4 and 6; Figures 4 and 5). These address mechanisms and portability absent from v1. Conversely, v1's targeted RPE analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its empirical comparisons. Reported dataset averages remain unaccompanied by uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Reported Replica mean ATE changes from 0.32 to 0.28 cm for the proposed method and 0.39 to 0.36 cm for SplaTAM; the proposed method's ScanNet 0181 ATE changes from 8.74 to 9.53 cm. Transfer, ablation and convergence results are added; RPE and novel-view entries disappear. Runtime FPS changes from 0.31/0.43 to 0.49/1.41 despite unchanged per-frame times. Revised TUM/ScanNet averages cover expanded scene sets and are not direct same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the explicit smoothed-loss expression L_smooth(theta) = L(K * R(theta)) and corrects the densification-mask definition. Most existing equations are retained or reordered. The new Graduated Non-Convexity discussion and toy landscape provide conceptual motivation, without a theorem or convergence proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, four contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: temporary adaptive smoothing through CB-KNN improves tracking robustness while preserving mapping quality, remains compatible with existing frameworks and operates selectively on keyframes.

C2.justification: v2 develops a new loss-landscape/GNC interpretation, attributing robustness to avoiding sharp local minima. It assigns distinct geometric and appearance roles to position and color smoothing, interprets MonoGS results as evidence of wider applicability, and attributes runtime gains to approximately 40% fewer iterations. These materially expand the causal interpretation; no substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: CUDA integration, A40 hardware and principal smoothing hyperparameters remain documented. v2 removes v1's explicit 40 tracking/60 mapping iteration budgets and several implementation details, including first-frame initialization, current/latest/top-overlap keyframe selection and mapping's SSIM term. These are losses of documentation rather than established implementation changes.

R1.justification: The literature context is substantially refocused. Numerous segmentation and point-cloud-network citations disappear, while references including Mip-Splatting, SA-GS, 2D Gaussian Splatting, Photo-SLAM, MG-SLAM, Hier-SLAM and GNC pose optimization appear. The new GNC connection further changes the method's conceptual positioning.

P1.justification: Related work is rewritten and consolidated from four subsections to three. Method explanations are extensively rewritten and reordered, and experiments are reorganized around tracking, transfer, convergence and ablations. Terminology and author/affiliation information also change, while the abstract and conclusion remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The pipeline is redrawn, the opening trajectory figure is replaced by a conceptual landscape, and trajectory/rendering panels are redesigned. Tracking tables are split, runtime tables merged, and transfer, ablation and convergence displays added; RPE and novel-view tables are removed.

improvement.justification: The component ablations and MonoGS transfer test materially strengthen evidence for CB-KNN's mechanism and portability. However, removing RPE, novel-view and broad real-data rendering comparisons weakens other important validation, while implementation details are lost. The revised FPS and fewer-iteration claims are also unreconciled with unchanged per-frame timings in Table 5. These substantive gains and unresolved evidentiary losses prevent a reliable net assessment of overall quality.
